summary.title: Build a Command Line app with Go: lolcat
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a Go CLI that rainbow-colors text using ANSI 24-bit escape codes and a sine-based rgb() function, working as a stdin pipe.
takeaways: Color terminal output by prefixing characters with the ANSI escape sequence \033[38;2;R;G;Bm and resetting with \033[0m.
Generate a smooth rainbow by computing RGB values from sine waves offset by 2π/3, indexed by character position.
Make a Go program work as a pipe by reading os.Stdin with bufio.Reader.ReadRune until io.EOF.
Detect a terminal with os.ModeCharDevice to show usage help when no piped input is given.
Install the tool system-wide with go install, using the module name as the command name.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a lolcat clone in Go in stages. It starts by printing fake hacker phrases from the faker package, then adds a single gold-colored output using ANSI 24-bit escape codes. Next it introduces an rgb() function based on sine waves, adapted from the original Ruby lolcat, to produce a rainbow across characters. Finally it turns the program into a stdin pipe, first buffering runes and then coloring each rune as it is read, and notes that go install makes it a system-wide command.
